In January 2024 Kaspi.kz, a payments, shopping and banking company from Kazakhstan, listed its shares on the Nasdaq exchange in New York. It was a rare global listing for a firm from Central Asia.

Kaspi grew out of a small bank. Over the 2010s it turned into a super app: one phone app that most adults in the country use to pay bills, send money, shop online, book travel and take loans. Shops pay to sell through it, and the company earns from both sides. Its shares had first been sold in London in 2020.

Kaspi shows how far life in Kazakhstan has moved from cash since independence from the Soviet Union, and how fintech can leap ahead in countries without old card networks. Its model is often compared with China's Alipay.
